attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite endpoint heat-kernel group integral Z_v(s z) has not yet been evaluated, and a regulator-uniform sixth source derivative bound M_6 plus endpoint-tail bound tau_end is still missing.
steps: Fix the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator and isolate each reflected Wilson hairpin endpoint in a box B_v of width epsilon.
Represent endpoint Wilson variations by singlet flux sources J, parallel transported to one endpoint color frame; the connected four-flux cumulant is the fourth derivative of log Z_v(J).
Decompose the second boundary-OPE polarization into Wick-square, straight f f commutator, endpoint irreducible kappa_4, and endpoint-tail pieces.
Use the known cancellation: the Wick-square term is a positive Gram form, and the straight f f term is proportional to the null incidence on each straight shared segment, hence vanishes there.
Localize the remaining irreducible connected part to endpoint boxes and write it as K_v^sing[z_v] with the prefactor (g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and incidence norm I_v.
Replace the formal fourth derivative by the computable central difference D_h log Z_v; Taylor expansion gives the explicit error h^2 M_6/6.
Compare the certified negative endpoint contribution plus tau_end with the positive finite Schur-Feshbach margin M_G to obtain a promotion inequality and a demotion falsifier inequality.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The reduction is valid conditional on source differentiability and localization, but no numerical or analytic sign bound for the actual K_v^sing spectrum has been proved yet.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Endpoint kappa_4 source-difference certificate for reflected Wilson hairpins

assumptions: Endpoint boxes B_v of size epsilon isolate all non-straight Wilson sheet collisions, and their complements are included in a tail tau_end.
The heat-kernel lattice action is reflection positive and admits source derivatives up to order six on |s|<=2h uniformly in the endpoint box.
The null-channel incidence vector has zero straight-segment incidence, so the local f f commutator contact vanishes away from endpoints.
The Wick-square part of the connected Wilson contraction is a positive Gram contribution and is not used to create a negative estimate.
The corrected finite Schur-Feshbach H,K gate has positive margin M_G for the locked finite block.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet endpoint-box partition functions Z_{v,a,epsilon}(J) with singlet Wilson four-flux sources parallel transported to the endpoint frame.
target object: a regulator-uniform signed bound for the connected boundary-OPE polarization R_endpoint entering the corrected second-order Wilson OS gate.
controlled interface: central fourth source differences D_h log Z_v and sixth-cumulant error bounds controlling the negative spectrum of K_v^sing.

same-theory condition: the sources are infinitesimal variations of the locked Wilson plaquette-sheet observables, with no added boundary counterterm, no changed loop renormalization, and the same heat-kernel regulator used in H,K.
K_v^sing[z] is the irreducible connected singlet four-flux cumulant localized in endpoint box B_v along normalized incidence-color source z.
M_G denotes the already computed positive corrected Schur-Feshbach margin of the finite hairpin block, without restating its threshold formula.

equations.valid_when: Applies when z is a normalized endpoint incidence-color source supported inside one heat-kernel endpoint box.

equations.valid_when: Valid when ell_v is six times differentiable on the source segment |s|<=2h with bounded sixth derivative.

equations.valid_when: Requires the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet Wilson expansion with null incidence cancellation on every straight shared segment.

equations.valid_when: Applies after the H,K Schur-Feshbach gate supplies a positive margin M_G for the locked finite block.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A negative certified central fourth difference whose color-geometric prefactor beats M_G is a genuine same-theory falsifier; failure of the sixth-derivative or tail bound means the certificate is not valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the remaining R/kappa_4 endpoint problem into a finite signed source-derivative computation with rigorous error bars, instead of a symbolic R_ij placeholder.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Endpoint source-difference certificate. In the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator, after Wick-square Gram positivity and straight f f null-incidence cancellation, the post-H,K endpoint term is bounded by central fourth differences of local singlet source log partition functions. This gives a valid promotion or falsifier inequality against the positive Schur-Feshbach margin M_G.

assumptions: The endpoint fluxes are parallel transported to a common endpoint frame before color contraction.
The singlet projection is the same one induced by the traced fundamental Wilson loops.
The fourth cumulant is symmetric under exchange of the two source pairs after connected Wick pairings have been removed.
definitions: Pair index A=(alpha,p,a; beta,q,b) records two endpoint plaquette-sheet flux insertions after singlet color projection.
r_v(c)_A is the symmetric pair-incidence vector built from the finite Wilson coefficients c_alpha and local endpoint incidences eta_{alpha p}.
The matrix Kmat_v^sing has entries given by the connected four-flux source derivative of log Z_v, flattened in the pair indices.
I_v(c)=||r_v(c)||^2 is the endpoint incidence norm carrying the geometric multiplicity.

equations.label: flattened cumulant matrix
equations.valid_when: Valid when endpoint flux labels i,j,k,l use the same parallel-transported color frame.

equations.label: incidence spectral bound
equations.latex: \mathcal E_v(c)=\langle r_v(c),\mathsf K_v^{\mathrm{sing}}r_v(c)\rangle,\qquad -\mathcal E_v(c)\le I_v(c)\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\mathsf K_v^{\mathrm{sing}})\}
equations.valid_when: Applies after pair symmetrization and singlet projection convert the quartic Wilson contraction into a matrix form.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If flattening is not self-adjoint because the source insertion changes the Wilson observable algebra, the spectral bound is not a same-theory estimate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Identifies the color/geometric factors to compute: the Yang-Mills input is Kmat_v^sing, while T_F, N, and I_v are explicit prefactors.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Flattened endpoint spectral compression. The endpoint quartic cumulant can be evaluated as a finite self-adjoint matrix on symmetric pair sources; its negative eigenvalue gives a conservative bound for every null-channel Wilson incidence vector.

assumptions: Endpoint holonomies remain inside a heat-kernel injectivity neighborhood with uniformly controlled parametrix remainder.
The source z is normalized in the same endpoint incidence norm used in the spectral inequality.
No boundary OPE counterterm is inserted when passing from the plaquette source to the Wilson hairpin source.
definitions: t_v is the effective heat-kernel time seen by the endpoint-box plaquette source.
chi_v(z) is the endpoint quadratic susceptibility along the same source z.
C_A is the adjoint Casimir controlling the first nonabelian curvature correction.

equations.label: non-Gaussian remainder target
equations.valid_when: Valid when the heat-kernel endpoint parametrix is uniform on the whole source segment and large holonomies are negligible.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: An O(1) negative K_v^sing as t_v->0 would falsify the small-time diagnostic or reveal an unremoved endpoint boundary defect.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Explains why the finite-difference experiment should see only the true connected boundary-OPE polarization, not the leading Gaussian damping already handled by H.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Small-time diagnostic. The abelian Gaussian tangent heat-kernel law contributes no endpoint kappa_4, so the dangerous signed part is a non-Gaussian curvature or interaction cumulant. A parametrix bound of this remainder would promote the block without full diagonalization.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if Z_v(J) cannot be defined as a source derivative of the locked Wilson plaquette-sheet regulator without adding a boundary counterterm.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the certified bound (g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 sum_v I_v Lambda_{-,v}+|tau_end| is strictly below M_G uniformly along cutoff removal.
control_decision.reason: The branch is not looping: it produced a computable regulator-level estimator with explicit error bars for the actual endpoint kappa_4 spectrum.

dependency_updates.description: The corrected H,K gate is now compressed into a single positive margin M_G; no further obstruction-ladder restatement is needed.
The concrete block supplies the null-channel incidence vector and the positive margin against which endpoint kappa_4 is compared.
The actual Yang-Mills input is now the finite endpoint heat-kernel source log partition function at 0, +/-h, and +/-2h for incidence-color sources.
Needed to turn central fourth differences into rigorous upper and lower sign certificates.
Needed to ensure all non-straight residual connected boundary-OPE terms are included in tau_end below the Schur-Feshbach margin.

falsifiers: A computed central fourth source difference with certified negative part large enough to exceed M_G after the prefactor is a same-theory endpoint falsifier.
A nonzero straight f f contribution after checking the exact null incidence would falsify the claimed cancellation and reopen the H,K decomposition.
A sixth source derivative bound M_6 that diverges faster than the finite-difference signal as a->0 or epsilon->0 would make the certificate invalid.
If defining Z_v(J) requires a boundary counterterm or a Wilson-loop renormalization not present in H,K, the calculation is not same-theory.
Endpoint tails comparable to M_G after Wick-square and straight-contact cancellation would demote the endpoint-local reduction.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 248 does not repeat the prior threshold. It converts the remaining post-H,K R term into a finite endpoint source-derivative computation: D_h log Z_v estimates the singlet connected four-flux kappa_4 with an explicit h^2 M_6/6 error. The leading Gaussian part is killed by the fourth difference, Wick-square contractions are positive, and straight f f contacts cancel by null incidence. The only dangerous quantity is therefore a certified negative non-Gaussian endpoint cumulant plus tail, with a valid promotion/falsifier inequality against M_G.
